findings.title: Denial cache key collides with permission cache key
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`, while userPermCacheKey is `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>`. Both are stored in the same underlying cache, and the key spaces overlap. The key is also ambiguous because the parts are joined with '_' and names or actions may contain underscores. A denial entry could therefore collide with a permission entry, or with another user/resource combination. Fix by using a distinct prefix such as `.perm_denial_` and an unambiguous separator.

findings.title: Denial cache defeats the fix for newly created resources
findings.body: After a denial, the entry is cached for 30s under (user, action, name, parent). A user who checks a resource just before it is created, or before their permission is granted, stays denied for 30s even though the DB now allows access. Nothing invalidates the denial entry when permissions change. This undermines the stated goal of letting creators access resources they just created. Negative caching of denials for the same user and resource should be shorter or be invalidated on creation.

findings.title: Errors from the cached lookup are swallowed and metrics are skewed
findings.body: An error from getCachedIdentityPermissions is silently ignored, and the code falls through to the DB path. That path then repeats GetUserIdentifiers, so the same failure is hit twice. Separately, the permissionCacheUsage metric is incremented as a cache miss whenever the cached permissions are present but do not grant access, and also when the cache simply misses. The two cases are conflated. On a cache miss the DB path is always taken even when the miss is only a not-found result.

findings.title: Removed cache-hit test and unverified single-flight behavior
findings.body: The test case for returning permissions from the cache in getUserPermissions was deleted. The `cacheHit` field and its branch in that test are now dead code. There is also no test that a denial is written to the denial cache after a DB-confirmed deny, nor that List falls back to the DB on a cache miss.
